hypothesis: Record 61b1f3b's reported-only candidate: 'REFINE HARNESS SAVE ON EMPTY PLANS: the harness state save (write+fsync+rename) runs even when 0 edits applied (the empty-plan case measured) — skipping the save when the plan applies nothing saves one durable write per empty refine; TS-parity check first.' The lane's brief: (1) confirm the empty-plan save at the tip and measure its share of the refine path (256KiB controls), (2) implement the parity-safe cut (skip the save when the plan is empty AND the harness state is unchanged, the guard PROVING no-change), (3) the byte-identity differential oracle, or the honest negative. OUTCOME: the TS-parity check — the candidate's own stated precondition — REFUTES the cut before any product code. The empty-plan save is NOT a wasted byte-no-op rewrite: it is the write that persists the refinement event.
approach: MEASUREMENT ONLY, no product change (the honest-negative lane; the refutation is the deliverable). (1) CODE-LEVEL REFUTATION at the tip e2ee82f2d: apply_refinement_proposal UNCONDITIONALLY appends a HarnessRefinementEvent to the target state (pa-core refinement/planner.rs:439) — for the empty-edits plan too (the refine prompt explicitly solicits it: executor.rs:250 'Return only JSON edits. If no useful edit is justified, return an empty edits array with a rationale.'); execute_refinement then saves the FULL state including that event (session_engine/refine.rs:326 -> refinement/mod.rs:250 save_harness_state: to_string_pretty + '\n' via settings::storage::atomic_write = write(tmp,pid-suffixed) + sync_all + rename). TS is identical: agent-session.ts:10039 applyRefinementProposal -> refinement.ts:1142 state.refinements.push (unconditional) -> :10045 result.harnessStatePath = saveHarnessState(...) -> :399-405 JSON.stringify(state,null,2)+'\n' via writeFileAtomicSync({mode}). The event is user/model-visible: the harness digest renders it (ranking.rs:330 'recent refinements: N' + :341 changes:[] -> 'no applied edits' = TS refinement.ts:756/:765 the same strings) and rlm.get_harness_state exposes the refinements array. (2) RUNTIME CAMPAIGN on a fresh VM (hillclimb-perf-empty-plan-save, ubuntu:22.04 16c/32GB/100GB vm=True, rustup 1.98.1, cargo build --release --locked --workspace rc=0): the bench harness (settle: template + kernel-venv warm) with the offline mock (prime-inference/mock-1; the refiner queue returns the empty plan {summary:'bench',edits:[]} for every call); per-trial cold-resume legs over the REAL assembly with TWO sequential empty-plan refines per trial (cmd1: the file created with event #1; cmd2: the file-present rewrite with event #2 — the byte-no-op refutation evidence), the harness_state.json hashed+parsed before launch and after EVERY command, the full response data recorded (appliedEdits + harnessStatePath = the served-path assertion), session rows pre/post, arrival-accurate frame pump, per-command mock-log windows. Classes: small=session-256kib (the fixed-floor control, fleet sha bd18b080..., 190 rows), stock=session-10mib (the size-scaled control, dadaecfc..., 7391 rows), seeded=session-256kib + the realistic 705,444-byte harness state pre-seeded (sha 0cc5c3d2..., 296 memories + 10 prompts + 5 skills + 6 refinement events — the save's realistic-size cost + the entries-survival proof). Legs: block-interleaved timing A1(small) B1(stock) C1(seeded) C2(seeded) B2(stock) A2(small), 3 trials each (18 trials); census legs under strace -ff -f -tt -T (fd-mapped, path-classified) 2 trials per class (6 trials, structure + span evidence, INVALID for timing); I/O advisory v1.0 probe_v09 pre/mid/post + before EVERY block (12 probes, PHASE MODEL re-classified at every boundary, NO-CEILING); binary sha asserted at every block start+end (ae1b2a1b... unchanged throughout); quiet gate + product-only zombie sweep; per-trial fixture prehash assert.
parity_notes: No product source changed in any phase; frozen parity untouched (the RPC surface exercised as a black box over stdio). THE REFUTATION IS ITSELF THE PARITY FINDING, in two independent mechanisms: (1) EVENT APPEND: any candidate that skips the empty-plan save (or drops the event append to make the state 'unchanged') diverges the on-disk harness state from the TS reference — TS persists the same event through the same unconditional save (agent-session.ts:10045; refinement.ts:1142), and the harness digest + rlm.get_harness_state render the refinements array identically in both products (ranking.rs:330/341 = refinement.ts:756/765). The brief's byte-identity oracle (the harness-state file byte-identical across baseline/candidate in the empty-plan class) is therefore UNSATISFIABLE for any skip: the baseline's post-refine file always contains the fresh event (fresh id refine_<ts> + created_at), so the candidate must write it too — the write is load-bearing, and a guard that honestly proves no-change (byte-compare would-be content vs the on-disk file) NEVER fires for refine. (2) CROSS-WRITER NORMALIZATION: the save is also a format-normalizing write — a TS-written harness file (insertion-ordered entries) round-trips through the Rust writer to BTreeMap-sorted key order with identical entry semantics but reordered bytes (measured: the seeded 705,444-byte TS-written state -> the post-refine file's entries section byte-reorders while the canonicalized entries sha stays 5921887a...); so even a genuinely unchanged state is never a byte-no-op across writers. Neither mechanism touches a frozen surface (the file is a data store, not wire/TUI bytes); both make the skip class dead.

refutation_the_skip_class_is_dead.theorem: (1) apply_refinement_proposal appends a HarnessRefinementEvent with a fresh id (refine_<17 digits>) and fresh created_at to the target state on EVERY refine — empty plan included (planner.rs:439 = TS refinement.ts:1142). (2) save_harness_state serializes the FULL state (mod.rs:250/256 = TS refinement.ts:399-405). (3) Therefore the post-refine file always differs from the pre-refine file. (4) The brief's byte-identity oracle (baseline vs candidate, empty-plan class) requires the candidate's post-file to equal the baseline's post-file — which contains the event. (5) A skip that leaves the file's bytes unchanged cannot produce the event; therefore no skip satisfies the oracle; the guard that proves no-change (byte-compare) never fires. QED.
refutation_the_skip_class_is_dead.runtime_proof: the harness-file evidence above: 24/24 trials, file absent->created->rewritten (or 6->7->8 events seeded), shas distinct at every step
refutation_the_skip_class_is_dead.visibility_proof: the event renders in the harness digest ('[refine_x] <trigger>: no applied edits') and rides rlm.get_harness_state — dropping it is a user/model-visible divergence from TS, not an internal-only optimization
refutation_the_skip_class_is_dead.guard_verdict: an honest no-change guard would be DEAD CODE for the refine path (it can never fire); shipping it would green-fish the diff — the lane ships NOTHING
refutation_the_skip_class_is_dead.skip_class_future_readers: any future 'skip no-op saves' lane must FIRST prove the save is a byte-no-op — which this lane proves it NEVER is for refine: the event append changes the content every run (fresh id/created_at), and the cross-writer normalization (TS insertion-order -> Rust BTreeMap-sorted) reorders even a semantically-unchanged state. The only byte-stable case is a Rust-written file re-saved with an unchanged event list — impossible after any refine. The skip class is closed for refine; audit it per-call-site before reviving it anywhere else.

durability_finding_the_real_cost_is_a_po.finding: the harness save's measured cost is the fresh-file FSYNC — and the TS reference DOES NOT PERFORM IT. TS's writeFileAtomicSync (utils/atomic-file.ts:52) fsyncs the temp file only when options.fsync is passed (:65 'if (options.fsync) fsyncSync(descriptor)'), and the harness save passes only {mode} (refinement.ts:404) — write + atomic rename, NO fsync. So do the TS settings (settings-manager.ts:390 {mode: 0o600}) and auth writes (auth-storage.ts:206/250); only a few daemon-side paths opt in (e.g. rlm-subagent-display.ts:79 fsync:true). The Rust port's shared atomic_write (pa-core settings/storage.rs:~300: write_all + sync_all + rename) fsyncs ALWAYS — the port added durability uniformly. TS's session rows are plain appendFileSync (session-manager.ts:961/:2042 — no fsync at all) while the Rust port appends + fdatasyncs every row.
durability_finding_the_real_cost_is_a_po.measured_cost_of_the_addition: the save's fsync is the dominant term of the empty-plan refine in the D regime (25.3-34.6ms, size-independent 323B<->705KB, = the probe's A-regime wall; the write itself 10-33us, the rename 0.02-0.09ms); the session rows' fdatasyncs are mostly fast-path (0.15-4.9ms in-command) but stall at block-allocation boundaries (the boot rows paid 24-26ms each)
durability_finding_the_real_cost_is_a_po.candidate_class: a parity-ALIGNMENT candidate (NOT this lane's skip): match TS's per-call durability for the harness save — write+rename without the temp-fsync. The on-disk content is byte-identical, the write choreography order and all frozen surfaces unchanged; the semantics delta is the crash window: a power loss may lose the last harness-state write exactly as the TS reference does today. Expected saving: the D-regime save span 25-35ms -> ~0.03-0.09ms (the write+rename pair), i.e. the empty-plan refine wall -80% at 256KiB / -70% seeded / -22-30% at 10MiB; the healthy-regime saving ~1-1.5ms. SCOPE WARNING: settings::storage::atomic_write is the SHARED helper (settings/auth/harness all ride it in the port) — the lane must re-derive the durability contract per call site (TS's own call-site survey: settings/auth/harness all fsync-less; daemon journal/display paths fsync) and decide the port's crash-safety policy explicitly, with the merge bar's oracle discipline (the byte-identity of every store's content across baseline/candidate + the crash-window disclosure). TS-parity check FIRST, as this lane's refutation demonstrates.

outcome: HONEST NEGATIVE (the candidate is closed, refuted at code level and confirmed at runtime): the empty-plan harness save is NOT a wasted write — it is the write that persists the refinement event (changes: []) that both products append unconditionally and render in the harness digest; NO parity-safe skip exists in the empty-plan class (the byte-identity oracle is unsatisfiable for any skip; an honest no-change guard never fires), so no product change, no PR. The lane's second deliverable is the share measurement: in the D regime the save is the DOMINANT term of the empty-plan refine (~80% of the 256KiB wall, ~70% seeded, ~22-30% at 10MiB) and the cost decomposes to a port-side durability fsync the TS reference does not pay — reported as the follow-up candidate with its scope warning.
decision: The skip candidate from record 61b1f3b is CLOSED as refuted (do not revive without new evidence that the event append is dropped upstream — an upstream change that removes the empty-plan event WOULD reopen the skip class, and this record's oracle construction is the template). The measured share re-scopes the cost from 'one wasted durable write' to 'the dominant term of the empty-plan refine in the D regime, caused by the port's durability addition' — the follow-up candidate (TS-per-call-durability alignment for the harness save) is reported-only and needs its own lane: the shared atomic_write helper's contract must be re-derived per call site, the crash-window semantics disclosed, and the merge bar carried.
